content:
Appendix VI
(EXCERPTS FROM SAME TEXT-UPAPĪṬHA
प्रासादमण्टपादीनामुन्नतार्थं विशेषतः ।
शोभार्थं च समुद्दिष्टमुपपीठमतः श्रृणु ॥१॥
द्विगुणं तदधिष्ठानात्पादोनद्विगुणं तु वा ।
पञ्चांशं व्यंशकं वाथ भवेदर्धाधिकं तु वा ॥२॥
पादाधिकं समं वाथ त्रिपादं वापि कारयेत्।
कृत्वोत्सेधं दशांशं चाप्येकद्वित्रिमिरंशकैः ॥३॥
अधिष्ठानसमं बाह्ये निर्गमं त्रिविधं स्मृतम्।
त्रिद्वयेकदण्डमानं वा निर्गमं तत्त्रिधं भवेत्।॥४॥
उत्सेधे द्वादशांशे तु द्वाभ्यां पादुकमुच्यते ।
तदूवें पद्ममंशेन क्षेपणं चार्धभागतः ॥५॥
गलं भूतांशकं ज्ञेयं कम्पमर्धाशसमितम् ।
अंशेन पद्ममूर्ध्वं स्याद्वाजनं चांशकेन तु॥६॥
कम्पमंशेन कर्तव्यमेवष्टाङ्गसंमितम्।
अथवा तत्समुत्सेधे त्रिसप्तांशसमन्विते ॥७॥
नेत्रांशं पदुपानं स्याद्गुणांशं पद्ममुच्यते ।
व्योमांशं कन्धरं प्रोक्तं द्वाभ्यां वाजनमेव हि ॥८॥

Appendix VI ♦ 115
एकेन कम्पमष्टांशैः कर्णं तत्र प्रकल्पयेत्।
अंशेन कम्पमंशाभ्यां वाजनं कम्पमंशतः ॥९॥
कृत्वा षोडशधोदयं द्वयमितं कुर्यादुपानं तत-
स्तन्मानं कमलं च कम्पमथ तत्रैकन कर्णं ततः।
भूतांशैरथ कम्पमेकमुपरि द्वाभ्यां च पद्मं ततो
द्वाभ्यामेव हि पट्टिकां तदुपरि व्योमाशकं कम्पकम् ॥१०॥
कृत्वा सम्यगथोपपीठ उदयं चैकोनविंशांशंकं
द्वाभ्यां पादुकमम्बुजं द्वयमितं कम्पं शिवांशं भवेत्।
वस्वंशं गलमेकभागमथ तत्कम्पं च द्विद्व्यंशकं
पद्मं पट्टिकया भवेदुपरितः कम्पं खभागान्वितम्।॥११॥
कृत्वा वा मनुभागमम्बुजमिदं तत्पादुकं पङ्कजं
व्योमाशं त्वथ कम्पमर्धमथ षड्‌भागैर्गलं कम्पकम्।
अर्धं पुष्करभागमम्बुजमतो द्वाभ्यां भवेत्पट्टिका
कम्पं चोपरि तस्य भागसहितं तत्रोपपीठं भवेत् ॥१२॥
कण्ठे भूतगजव्यालसिंहयुक्तं यथा भवेत्।
तथा कुर्वीत मतिमान्यायुक्तमथापि वा ॥१३॥
उपपीठं समारव्यातं सर्वधाम्नां समासतः ॥१४॥
summary: This appendix contains excerpts from a Sanskrit architectural text detailing the design and proportions of the 'Upapīṭha', the pedestal or sub-base of a temple (prāsāda) or pavilion (maṇṭapa). The text outlines various proportional rules for the height of the Upapīṭha in relation to the main base (adhiṣṭhāna). It then describes several types of Upapīṭha by dividing their total height into a specific number of parts (e.g., 10, 12, 16, 19, 14 parts) and assigning these parts to a sequence of architectural mouldings like pāduka, padma, kampa, and gala. The final verses suggest that the kaṇṭha (neck) moulding can be adorned with sculpted figures of beings like bhūtas (sprites), gajas (elephants), vyālas (mythical creatures), and siṃhas (lions). The text concludes by stating that this is a brief description of the Upapīṭha applicable to all structures.
purpose: The purpose of this text is to provide a technical and prescriptive guide for sthapatis (traditional architects/builders) on the construction of the Upapīṭha. It establishes the canonical proportions, components, and potential ornamentation for this architectural element to ensure it is both structurally sound and aesthetically pleasing according to the principles of Vastu Shastra or Shilpa Shastra.
key_information: The Upapīṭha is a sub-base for structures like temples (prāsāda) and pavilions (maṇṭapa), intended for elevation and beautification.
Its height is defined proportionally to the main base (adhiṣṭhāna), with several possible ratios given (e.g., double, 1.75x, 1.5x, 1.25x, equal, 0.75x).
The text describes multiple types of Upapīṭha based on the number of vertical divisions (aṃśa or parts) of its total height, including systems of 10, 12, 16, 19, and 14 parts.
Specific names are given for the constituent horizontal mouldings, such as pāduka (footing), padma (lotus), kampa (fillet), gala/kaṇṭha (neck/recess), vājana, and paṭṭikā (band).
The kaṇṭha (neck moulding) can be decorated with carved figures of bhūtas (sprites), gajas (elephants), vyālas (mythical leonine creatures), and siṃhas (lions).
These principles are stated to be applicable to all types of buildings (sarvadhāmnāṃ).

tables_and_data.description: The verses contain proportional data for different types of Upapīṭha, defining the height of each moulding as a fraction of the total height. While not formatted as a table, this is the core quantitative information.
tables_and_data.data_summary: The text provides multiple proportional systems for constructing an Upapīṭha. For instance, a 12-part system is described (verses 5-6), where the total height is divided into 12 units and allocated to different mouldings: pāduka (2 parts), padma (1 part), kṣepaṇa (0.5 part), gala (4 parts), kampa (0.5 part), upper padma (1 part), and vājana (1 part). Similar breakdowns are provided for systems with 16 parts (verse 10), 19 parts (verse 11), and 14 parts (verse 12), each with a specific sequence and size of mouldings.
